what: Faults found in vr-08 that were deliberately NOT repaired when they were found, each with the reason. check:vr08-open-items measures every one from the rows on each run and reports OPEN or CLOSED, so an open item cannot decay into a forgotten one and cannot be closed silently.
rule: R992, R994 — a fault reported and not repaired is named here or it is lost

items.what: The vr-08 cut presents 25 rows built from 12 distinct word pairs. MOVE_LETTER_EXTRA holds 12 tuples and fromBank(bank, 25) cycles them, so CHAIR/MOP appeared three times and every other pair twice.
items.whyItWasNotRepaired: it is a defect in how the bank is EXPANDED, not in any pair. Repairing it means authoring thirteen more pairs or changing what fromBank does when the bank is short — both are content decisions, not a fix. R990 recorded that a duplicated population inflates every association computed over it, which is the cost already being paid.
items.whoseDecision: David and Annie — how a short bank should expand, or whether the cut should be twelve rows
items.measuredBy: distinct (word1, word2) pairs against row count across the vr-08 cut

items.what: seed-vr08-04 (COAT/HARD) has a letter that performs the task at the 3.0 cut, and it is not the letter recorded as the key. It works on O (COAT->CAT 4.83, HARD->HOARD 3.31); the key says C, which needs OAT (2.70) and CHARD (2.95) — both below the cut on BOTH instruments.
items.whyItWasNotRepaired: both rows are NEVER_SHIPPABLE and reach no child, and correcting a key is a content decision on rows the reviewer has already ruled out of service. Repairing them would also change rows that several crossed artefacts describe.
items.whoseDecision: Annie — whether a NEVER_SHIPPABLE seed row is corrected or left as the record of what was made
items.andWHYITISNAMEDSEPARATELY: UNPERFORMABLE and MIS-KEYED are different faults. The earlier count reported these two inside a single 'unperformable' figure, which is wrong about both: the stem is sound and the answer is wrong.
items.measuredBy: for each seed row, the letters that perform the task at the cut, against the recorded key
items.CORRECTED_2026_09_05: This item originally named seed-vr08-05 (BEAST/RING) as well. THAT WAS AN ARTEFACT OF THIS STORE'S OWN NAME FILTER, not a fault in the row: EAST reads 5.19 and was excluded as a proper noun, which made the recorded key B fail. The key B is correct — BEAST->EAST, RING->BRING, both far above the cut. The filter was repaired to compute Zipf from non-name frequency and the row is sound. Found by Annie's disagreement set, not by anything on this side alone.
